summary: Steady-stepoff emergency exit: assist with optimizer config audit and safe live rollback
description: Issue summary: LumaDocs deployed a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enables aggressive async-batching, KV prefix prefetch, and mixed-precision quantization. Post-deploy they report intermittent 5xxs and sustained 95p latency increase for long-session chat endpoints. Impact: production customer traffic affected for several routes; revenue-featuring workflows show 15-25% request errors and longer tail latency. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, tenant pinned to llama-2-70b-quant-v2 with optimizer profile 'aggr-opt-v3'. Request: Assistance auditing current optimizer config and an ordered, safe rollback plan that can be executed with minimal customer-visible disruption.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ana Patel: Customer reports spike in 5xxs after enabling profile 'aggr-opt-v3' yesterday. We need prioritized rollback guidance and an audit of which flags in the profile are likely culprits.

2026-03-10 10:03 - Diego Ramirez: Acknowledged. Initial plan: capture current runtime snapshot, isolate tenant traffic to a canary pool, and perform ordered demotion of optimizer features. Will request quick telemetry windows from SRE.

2026-03-11 08:27 - SRE (J. O'Connor): Telemetry collected - increase in inference queue depth correlating with async-batching bump and KV prefetch errors in worker logs. Attached traces: /dashboards/serving/us-east/tenant-lumadocs/trace-20260310.
2026-03-11 11:50 - Diego Ramirez: Shared step-by-step rollback plan below. Awaiting customer approval for traffic-split and short maintenance window.
2026-03-12 07:34 - Customer (LumaDocs) Support Lead: Approved. Would like minimal impact window 10:00-10:30 PDT today. Please confirm exact commands and expected monitoring signals.
investigation_notes: Observed symptom timeline: 2026-03-09 21:00 deploy of 'aggr-opt-v3' -> 2026-03-10 00:30 first 5xx spike, sustained elevated 95p latency through morning traffic peaks.

Hypothesis A: Async continuous batching increased queueing for long-session prompts causing worker timeouts under heavy concurrency. Evidence: queue_depth metric up 3x, request timeouts in worker logs.

Hypothesis B: KV prefix prefetch mis-indexed some tenant keys leading to cache-miss storms and backend DB pressure. Evidence: spike in kv-prefetch-errors and increased backend latency spikes recorded in tracing.

Hypothesis C: Mixed-precision quant profile introduced occasional numerical instability for long-session attention leading to 5xx internal errors. Evidence: a subset of 5xx stack traces reference kernel NaN checks and forced fallback exceptions.
Telemetry links: traces (https://dash.redwood.ai/traces/us-east/trace-20260310), metrics: serving/latency/tenant/lumadocs, logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/lumadocs/2026-03-10/

Risk assessment: Full instant revert of model binary may cause cold-cache latency spike but will likely reduce 5xxs fastest. Ordered feature demotion is lower risk to correctness but may take longer to validate behavior under load.
resolution_notes: Approved rollback window 2026-03-12 10:00-10:30 PDT. Executed steps below in sequence and verified signals at each step.

Step 0 (snapshot): Took live optimizer-config snapshot and stored under s3://config-snapshots/lumadocs/2026-03-12/aggr-opt-v3-snapshot.json. Created serving runtime snapshot with command: redwoodctl snapshot create --tenant lumadocs --note 'pre-rollback 2026-03-12'.

Step 1 (traffic isolation): Performed temporary traffic split (90% -> stable pool, 10% -> original) to validate rollback steps against reduced blast radius. Command: redwoodctl traffic-split set --tenant lumadocs --routes '/chat/*' --split 'stable:90,orig:10'. Observed stable pool 95p latency remained within SLA during tests.

Step 2 (demote async-batching): Disabled async-batching features in tenant profile (flags: async_batching=true -> false). Command: redwoodctl config set --tenant lumadocs --profile aggr-opt-v3 --patch '{"async_batching":false}'. Monitoring: queue_depth returned to baseline within 3 minutes; 5xxs reduced by ~60%.

Step 3 (evict defective KV prefetch): Temporarily disabled kv_prefix_prefetch and evicted tenant KV entries: redwoodctl config set --tenant lumadocs --patch '{"kv_prefix_prefetch":false}'; redwoodctl cache evict --tenant lumadocs --scope kv_prefix --confirm. Backend latency normalized.

Step 4 (fallback quantized model): For sanity, pinned tenant back to fp16 model variant for graceful correctness: redwoodctl model pin --tenant lumadocs --from "llama-2-70b-quant-v2" --to "llama-2-70b-fp16" --reason 'rollback for stability'. Expected impact: slight cost increase, reduction in rare numeric exceptions. Verified 5xxs subsided to <1% and 95p latency within baseline.

Step 5 (gradual rollback completion): After 20 minutes of stable metrics, ramped traffic back to 100% on stable pool and removed temporary traffic-split. Cleaned up snapshot labels and documented the rollback in customer ticket.

Post-mortem action items: 1) Create a canary gating rule for async-batching with queue_depth threshold and automatic demotion. 2) Add KV prefetch integrational test for tenant key namespace collisions. 3) Re-evaluate quantization regression tests for long-session attention patterns. Assigned to: Research/Applied ML (K. Wu), SRE (J. O'Connor), Platform (D. Ramirez).

Follow-up notes to customer: Provided a short writeup with the exact patch commands, snapshot location, and recommended safer rollout steps for future experiments: incremental per-route canaries, 5-minute staging windows, and preflight synthetic load tests.
